subtitle: When Rumour Lit a City and an Empire Bled

panels.shot: high wide shot over Shahjahanabad at dusk, domes and minarets under a looming storm, Nader Shah's troops like dark ants in the streets
panels.action: Muhammad Shah Rangila stands on a high terrace of the Red Fort, his silken robes heavy, watching in helpless dread as Afsharid soldiers pour through the lanes of Shahjahanabad and smoke curls over the city.

dialogue.text: In March 1739, as Nader Shah ruled Delhi for a few days, a rumour, a riot and six hours of slaughter burned a mark no emperor’s pleasure could erase.

i18n.hi: मार्च 1739 में, जब नादिर शाह कुछ ही दिनों को दिल्ली का मालिक बना, एक अफवाह, एक फसाद और छह घंटे के कत्लेआम ने ऐसा दाग छोड़ा जिसे कोई बादशाही ऐश नहीं मिटा सकी।

panels.shot: slow push-in from a map-like bird’s-eye of North India down to the walled city of Shahjahanabad
panels.action: A parchment-like view shows the Yamuna, the walled oval of Shahjahanabad, the Red Fort on the river, the Jama Masjid’s domes rising above tight-packed houses, with small Afsharid camp fires flickering beyond the walls.

dialogue.text: By early 1739, Shahjahanabad still glowed with Mughal splendour, but its armies lay broken. Nader Shah, victor outside Karnal, now camped at its very heart.

i18n.hi: 1739 की शुरुआत तक शाहजहानाबाद अब भी मुगल शानो-शौकत से चमक रहा था, पर उसकी फ़ौजें चकनाचूर थीं। करनाल के विजेता नादिर शाह अब शहर के दिल में डेरा डाले बैठा था।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in the Diwan-i-Khas, low angle on throne, wide to show Persian presence
panels.action: Muhammad Shah Rangila sits on the Peacock Throne in the Diwan-i-Khas, shoulders slumped, while Nader Shah, in a plain but stern Persian coat and high cap, stands beside him, his guards lined up with cold discipline; Delhi courtiers look on anxiously.

dialogue.text: Inside the Red Fort, the Mughal emperor shared his own hall with the Persian conqueror. For now, as Anand Ram Mukhlis notes, Nader demanded obedience, not yet blood.

i18n.hi: लाल क़िले के भीतर, मुगल बादशाह ने अपना दीवान भी फ़ारसी फ़तह के मालिक से बाँट रखा था। अभी, जैसा आनंद राम मुख़लिस लिखता है, नादिर आज्ञा चाहता था, खून नहीं।

panels.shot: street-level tracking shot through Chandni Chowk, slightly low angle to show bustle and foreign troops
panels.action: Afsharid soldiers in distinctive caps and coats patrol Chandni Chowk, eyeing the crowded bazaar; Delhi shopkeepers sit tensely by their wares as women and children hurry past, and a few curious youths watch the invaders.

dialogue.text: Outside, Persian troops quartered in the bazaars and mohallas. They took supplies, demanded payment, and moved in alien silence through lanes that had known only Mughal guards.

i18n.hi: बाहर, फ़ारसी सिपाही बाज़ारों और मुहल्लों में डेरा डाले थे। राशन उठाते, पैसे वसूलते और उन गलियों में अजनबी सन्नाटे से गुजरते जो अब तक सिर्फ़ मुग़ल पहरेदारों की थीं।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot in a small Delhi home, candlelit, faces in half-shadow
panels.action: In a cramped upper room, a Delhi family huddles around a dim lamp; an elder whispers with worry while a younger man clenches his fists, listening to distant marching outside the shuttered window.

dialogue.text: Delhi’s people watched and waited. Some, like Mukhlis, recorded each new insult. Others only clenched their jaws and prayed the storm would pass over their roofs.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली वाले बस देखते और टकटकी लगाए बैठे रहे। कुछ, जैसे मुख़लिस, हर नई बेअदबी लिखते गए। बाक़ी दाँत भींचकर बस दुआ करते रहे कि तूफ़ान उनकी छतों से टकराकर निकल जाए।

panels.shot: dynamic street corner shot, mid-level, capturing first flare of violence
panels.action: On a narrow lane, an Afsharid soldier roughly shoves a Delhi porter aside while snatching goods; in the background, a small knot of local men exchange angry glances, one gripping a concealed club under his shawl.

dialogue.text: Tensions grew. Indo-Persian chroniclers speak of quarrels over money and honour, of soldiers taking what they wished in a city that lived on trade and pride.

i18n.hi: तनाव बढ़ता गया। हिन्द-फ़ारसी तारीख़नवीस रुपयों और इज़्ज़त की झड़पों का ज़िक्र करते हैं, उन सिपाहियों का जो उस शहर में मनमानी कर रहे थे जो सौदे और स्वाभिमान पर जीता था।

panels.shot: crowded market square shot, overhead oblique angle, chaos beginning
panels.action: In a bustling market square, an Afsharid officer lies collapsed on the cobbles, eyes closed; a few Delhi townsmen stand over him, faces flushed, while the crowd around them is a swirl of shock, fear and secret satisfaction.

dialogue.text: Then, as later accounts agree, word raced through the bazaars: Nader Shah is dead. Whether from a scuffle, a misstep or pure rumour, the spark caught dry grass.

i18n.hi: फिर, जैसा बाद की रिवायतें कहती हैं, ख़बर बाज़ारों में दौड़ गई: नादिर शाह मारा गया। मारपीट की, फिसलन की या महज़ अफवाह की, जो भी हो, चिंगारी सूखी घास पर जा गिरी।

panels.shot: fast, kinetic street-level shot with sharp diagonals, conveying erupting fury
panels.action: Delhi residents, some with sticks, others with household blades or stones, surge through a lane towards scattered Afsharid soldiers who look up in alarm; dust rises, a pot falls from a balcony, a child is hurried indoors by a mother at a doorway.

dialogue.text: Believing the conqueror fallen, groups of townspeople fell upon isolated Persian bands. Anand Ram notes that in some quarters, Afsharid soldiers were attacked and cut down amidst cries of sudden courage.

i18n.hi: फ़तह के बादशाह को मरा मानकर, शहर के झुंड, अलग-थलग फ़ारसी दलों पर टूट पड़े। आनंद राम लिखता है कि कई मुहल्लों में अफ़्शार सिपाहियों पर झपटकर, अचानाक उमड़ी हिम्मत की चीखों के बीच उन्हें काट गिराया गया।

panels.shot: wide city-lane shot, slightly elevated, to show scattered skirmishes without graphic detail
panels.action: Across several lanes visible from a rooftop vantage, Afsharid soldiers are seen being overwhelmed or fleeing down alleys while Delhi men block paths, hurling stones and wielding staffs; smoke begins to rise from a distant corner.

dialogue.text: Contemporary estimates speak of thousands of Persian soldiers killed in these sudden clashes. Yet the resistance was scattered, brief, and soon met an answering fury.

i18n.hi: हमज़माना बयान कहते हैं कि इन छिटपुट झड़पों में हज़ारों फ़ारसी सिपाही मारे गए। मगर ये बग़ावत बिखरी हुई, थोड़ी देर की थी, और जल्दी ही उसके जवाब में तूफ़ान टूट पड़ा।

panels.shot: interior wide shot in a temporary Persian headquarters, focus on a messenger and Nader Shah
panels.action: In a commandeered mansion room, a Persian messenger kneels breathless before Nader Shah, who stands rigid, face darkening as he listens; behind him, commanders exchange grim looks.

dialogue.text: When news of the killings reached Nader, the tone of his rule in Delhi changed. The chroniclers agree on what followed, though their numbers differ.

i18n.hi: जब नादिर तक इन क़त्लों की ख़बर पहुँची, दिल्ली में उसकी बादशाहत का लहजा बदल गया। तारीख़नवीस आगे की बात पर मुतफ़िक़ हैं, बस गिनती में फ़र्क़ पड़ता है।

panels.shot: exterior wide shot of Sunehri Masjid in Chandni Chowk, slight low angle, massed troops below
panels.action: Nader Shah stands on the roof or upper balcony of the Sunehri Masjid in Chandni Chowk, his figure rigid against the sky, while ranks of Afsharid soldiers look up from the square, hands on weapons, awaiting his signal.

dialogue.text: He rode to the Sunehri Masjid in Chandni Chowk. From there, say Abdul Karim and Rustam Ali, the order went out over the crowded square: a general massacre, qatl-i-am.

i18n.hi: वो चाँदनी चौक की सुनेहरी मस्जिद तक घोड़ा दौड़ाता पहुँच गया। वहीं से, अब्दुल करीम और रुसतम अली लिखते हैं, ठसाठस भरे चौक पर हुक्म गूँज गया: आम क़त्ल, क़त्ल-ए-आम।

panels.shot: tight, dramatic close-up on Nader Shah’s raised arm and hard-set face, city blurred behind
panels.action: Nader Shah’s arm is frozen mid-gesture as he raises his hand toward the city, his eyes narrowed, jaw clenched; behind him the hazy outline of rooftops and domes stretches away.

dialogue.text: Eyewitnesses describe no long debate, no softening. In his eyes, the killing of his men by Delhi’s people demanded an answer that would not be forgotten.

i18n.hi: आँखों देखा हाल कहता है, न कोई लंबी बहस हुई, न नर्मी। उसकी नज़र में, दिल्ली वालों द्वारा उसके सिपाहियों का खून ऐसा सवाल था जिसका जवाब भुलाया न जा सके।

panels.shot: sweeping overhead shot over a Delhi neighbourhood, soldiers fanning out like a dark flood
panels.action: Afsharid detachments pour into lanes from multiple directions, their lines curved like dark streams through the white and sandstone houses; doors slam, some figures flee across flat rooftops, others cower in courtyards.

dialogue.text: For hours, Persian troops swept through Shahjahanabad’s lanes. Indo-Persian and European reports alike speak of a city where, in many quarters, the invaders met little organised resistance.

i18n.hi: घंटों तक फ़ारसी गिरोह शाहजहानाबाद की गलियों में बहते रहे। हिन्द-फ़ारसी और यूरोपीय लिखतें एक ऐसी दिल्ली की बातें करती हैं जहाँ कई हिस्सों में हमलावरों को ढंग की कोई संगठित मज़ाहमत नहीं मिली।

panels.shot: mid-level lane shot focusing on civilians’ terror and submission rather than combat
panels.action: In a narrow lane, a group of unarmed townspeople—men, women, children—kneel or huddle in fear as Afsharid soldiers stride past; one old man lifts his hands in appeal, while a young man glares, held back by family.

dialogue.text: Mukhlis writes that a few offered opposition, but most were cut down or seized where they stood, unable or unwilling to fight trained soldiers in the maze of their own streets.

i18n.hi: मुख़लिस लिखता है, कुछ लोगों ने टक्कर दी, पर ज़्यादातर वहीं के वहीं काट दिए गए या गिरफ़्तार हुए, अपनी ही गलियों की भूलभुलैया में पेशेवर फ़ौज से भिड़ने की हिम्मत या हुनर के बिना।

panels.shot: interior courtyard shot, intimate, emphasizing loss and fear
panels.action: Inside a small Haveli courtyard, a woman clutches a child to her chest as an Afsharid soldier drags away a young man; another soldier glances into a room where valuables are hastily hidden under a mat.

dialogue.text: Alongside the killing came seizure. Chroniclers and foreign letters speak of looting and the taking of captives, as houses were forced open and families broken apart.

i18n.hi: क़त्ल के साथ छीना-झपटी भी चली। तारीख़ें और बाहरी ख़त लूट, गिरफ़्तारी और घरों के उज़ड़ने का ज़िक्र करते हैं, जब दरवाज़े तोड़कर खानदानों को अलग कर दिया गया।

panels.shot: wide, smoky cityscape shot at a distance, showing fires and stillness after chaos
panels.action: A view from a far rooftop shows patches of smoke drifting over parts of the city, scattered fires smouldering; the streets below are oddly still, with occasional Afsharid patrols moving through the haze.

dialogue.text: By the time Nader called off the slaughter, perhaps tens of thousands lay dead by varying accounts. Delhi’s noise, once of trade and song, fell into a stunned, smoky silence.

i18n.hi: जब तक नादिर ने क़त्ल-ए-आम रुकवाया, अलग-अलग बयान के हिसाब से शायद दर्जनों हज़ार लोग ज़मीं पर पड़े थे। सौदे और गीतों से गूँजती दिल्ली की आवाज़ अब सन्नाटे और धुएँ में घुल गई।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of the Diwan-i-Am or a hall in the Red Fort, wide and echoing
panels.action: Muhammad Shah stands with a few shaken nobles in an almost empty hall, their faces drawn; beyond the arches, lines of Delhi residents, some bandaged or veiled in mourning, slowly enter the fort to seek redress.

dialogue.speaker: muhammad_shah_and_delhi_s_residents
dialogue.text: How does a king answer his people when words come too late?

i18n.hi: जब ज़बान देर से खुले, तो बादशाह अपने लोगों को क्या जवाब दे?

panels.shot: opulent interior shot of the Peacock Throne being dismantled, focus on artisans and soldiers
panels.action: Afsharid soldiers and workmen carefully dismantle the Peacock Throne under watchful officers; jewelled panels and encrusted figures are carried away, while in the background chests of coins and gems are stacked.

dialogue.text: In the days that followed, the qatl-i-am gave way to organised plunder. The Peacock Throne was stripped and carried off, and treasures like the Koh-i-Noor passed into Nader’s possession.

i18n.hi: अगले ही दिनों में क़त्ल-ए-आम की जगह बक़ायदा लूट ने ले ली। तख़्त-ए-ताउस उधेड़कर उठा लिया गया, और कोहिनूर जैसे ख़ज़ाने नादिर की झोली में चले गए।

panels.shot: grand riverbank shot of Nader Shah’s camp breaking along the Yamuna, with long columns readying to depart
panels.action: On the banks of the Yamuna, endless columns of pack animals and wagons stand laden with chests and fabrics; Afsharid banners flutter as soldiers prepare to march, while distant city walls glimmer under the sun.

dialogue.text: Nader Shah also fixed an immense indemnity, forcing Delhi and the court to yield yet more wealth. When his army finally left, it carried away fortunes that had taken generations to build.

i18n.hi: नादिर शाह ने एक भारी भरकम मुआवज़ा भी ठोंक दिया, दिल्ली और दरबार को और दौलत उगलने पर मजबूर किया। जब उसकी फ़ौज आख़िर चली, तो सदियों की जमा पूँजी बोरियों में भरकर ले गई।

panels.shot: quiet, low-angle street shot years later, with repaired but aged buildings, focus on survivors
panels.action: Years later, an older Delhi resident sits by a repaired doorway, telling attentive youths about that March; behind them, the Jama Masjid and houses still stand, patched and worn, as people move through the bazaar again.

dialogue.text: For the survivors, Delhi was never the same. Yet life crept back into its lanes, and stories of the six hours when the city bled were passed down with a mixture of grief and hard memory.

i18n.hi: बचे हुओं के लिए दिल्ली फिर कभी वैसी नहीं रही। फिर भी, ज़िंदगी धीरे-धीरे गलियों में लौट आई, और शहर के वो छह घंटे, जब दिल्ली खून में नहाई, ग़म और कड़वी याद के साथ कहानी बनकर पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी चलते रहे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a manuscript page being written, candlelight flickering, hand steady
panels.action: A scholar’s hand writes carefully in flowing Persian script on a manuscript page, the ink glistening; beside him lie other bound volumes and a small window shows a sliver of the city beyond.

dialogue.text: Because men like Anand Ram Mukhlis and Abdul Karim wrote what they saw and heard, Delhi’s six hours of blood cannot be wished away. Their ink keeps both resistance and ruin from fading into legend.

i18n.hi: क्योंकि आनंद राम मुख़लिस और अब्दुल करीम जैसे लोगों ने जो देखा-सुना, उसे लिख छोड़ा, दिल्ली के छह घंटे का खून अब मिटाया नहीं जा सकता। उनकी स्याही ने बग़ावत और बरबादी, दोनों को दास्तानों में घुलने से बचा लिया।

title_i18n.hi: दिल्ली के छह घंटे का खून

subtitle_i18n.en: When Rumour Lit a City and an Empire Bled
subtitle_i18n.hi: अफवाह ने शहर भड़काया, साम्राज्य खून से नहाया
